name: The Great Stink: a sample script with two failures a person named
audience: Curious viewers who know London but not its sewers.
central_question: Why did London act on its sewage only when Parliament could smell it?

units.text: In the summer of 1858, the members of Parliament could not breathe.
The MBW had been warned for years, and still nothing moved.
Every flushing toilet in London emptied, in the end, into the Thames.
People believed bad air carried disease, so the smell itself felt like a death sentence.
Within weeks, the same Parliament that had argued for a decade paid for a new system of sewers.
So what does it take for a problem to be fixed, rather than merely known?

expected.note: 'The MBW' is never said in full or explained
'argued for a decade' about what? The argument was never set up
